_comment: PLAT-37 / PARITY-P1 readings, pass of 2026-10-19 (clock 2026-10-17 EEST).
THE PASS'S SUBJECT: ground the advance comparison by recording the face each
renderer RESOLVED on each arm, then decide whether the two arms use the same
font file and, if they do, where the progressive drift comes from.
BOTH QUESTIONS ARE ANSWERED. The arms use THE SAME FILE, and the drift is
NOT a glyph-advance difference: it is a per-TEXT-ELEMENT width ceiling in the
vendored gpui-pre crate. Per the brief, a cause inside that pinned crate is
reported and not forked, so NO FIX WAS ATTEMPTED and P1 is unchanged.
Every number below was measured this pass unless marked carriedForward.

gpui.whyMETRICSandNOTaNAME: GPUI's TextSystem hands back a FontId and NO way to ask which file it came from -- `get_font_for_id` returns the REQUESTED `Font` key, so a name read back there would be the request echoed. unitsPerEm and the per-character advances are read THROUGH that id from the loaded face, so they are properties of the FILE. They are also the only property of it the advance question turns on.

theCONTROL.detail: the bogus family resolves through the fallback stack to a face with unitsPerEm **2048** and PROPORTIONAL advances (M 13.328, i 3.555). Space Mono is unitsPerEm **1000** and monospaced (M = i = W = 0 = 9.792). A probe echoing its input could not produce a different unitsPerEm for a name no font has. THE CONTROL IS INSIDE THE REPORT, on every capture, rather than run once beside it.
theCONTROL.andItIsNOTuniform: three queried families, three distinct fingerprints: 1000/0.612/mono, 1000/0.864/proportional, 2048/0.833/proportional. The uniformity ACROSS THE SEVEN VIEWS is expected and is not the axis the control tests -- every view is the same process with the same files.

theSameFileQuestion.verdict: YES -- THE SAME FILE, and it is named on both sides.
theSameFileQuestion.theCSSside: src/frontend/styles/generated/fonts.styl:44-51 declares @font-face family "SpaceMono" with src url('.../libs/codetracer-design-system/SpaceGrotesk_Complete/Fonts/Space_Mono/SpaceMono-Regular.ttf'). Blink confirms it took it: isCustomFont true, postScriptName SpaceMono-Regular.
theSameFileQuestion.theGPUIside: src/frontend/gpui/design_fonts.nim registers MonoFiles = SpaceMono-{Regular,Bold,Italic,BoldItalic}.ttf, resolved this run to the same .../Fonts/Space_Mono/ directory, as the report's registeredFiles prints verbatim.
theSameFileQuestion.theFileITSELF: read directly out of the TTF: unitsPerEm 1000, numberOfHMetrics 747, exactly two distinct advanceWidths {0, 612}, name table family 'Space Mono', PostScript name 'SpaceMono-Regular'. So the advance is 612/1000 em = 9.792 px at 16 px = 19.584 device px at 2x.
theSameFileQuestion.aTRAPthatDIDnotFIRE: design_fonts.nim's header warns that the `WEB/fonts/*.ttf` the stylesheet loads carry a broken name table (family literally `false`) and that the OTF builds are registered instead. That is TRUE FOR SPACE GROTESK and FALSE FOR SPACE MONO: the stylesheet's SpaceMono src points at Fonts/Space_Mono/, not at WEB/fonts/, which is the same directory design_fonts registers. The interface face therefore IS a different file on the two arms (WEB ttf vs OTF) and the CODE face is not. Only the code face matters for the editor drift; the interface face is left as an open question below.

theDriftLadder._rule: the brief's direct test, re-measured. FLIP_DIR has no default, so a frame directory inherited from another pass cannot be read by accident.
theDriftLadder.instrument: build/plat37-parity-2026-10-19/advance.py, with a least-squares slope added -- a monotone sequence of integers is read by eye, its slope is a number.
theDriftLadder.itREPRODUCES: editorWithMark's ladder is BIT-IDENTICAL to the 2026-10-18b pass's. The drift is real, reproducible and unchanged.
theDriftLadder.butTHEslopeDISAGREESbetweenPANES: 0.970% / 0.727% / 0.303%. A per-glyph advance difference in one face at one size is ONE number; three panes cannot disagree about it by a factor of three. That, with the direct advance measurement, is what sent this pass to a per-ROW ladder.

thePerRowLadder._whyItWasRUN: the pane-level ladder sums EVERY row into one profile. rowextent.py found 5 to 12 bands per pane whose GPUI first-ink is 74-79 device px RIGHT of Electron's, so the pane sum mixes rows at different offsets, and a changing mix can drag a local best-fit shift with no glyph moving progressively. The per-row ladder separates the two.
thePerRowLadder.result: THE MIXING EXPLANATION IS REFUTED: individual rows DO drift. editorWithMark, 21 rows with a usable ladder, per-row shift running +0 -> +6 device px WITHIN ONE ROW.
thePerRowLadder.andTHISisTHEkey: the per-row slopes are DISCRETE, not continuous: 0.000, 0.278, 0.813, 0.833, 1.071, 1.290, 1.349, 1.369, 1.667 percent. Several rows drift EXACTLY ZERO. A per-glyph advance error cannot produce a zero row and cannot produce a discrete ladder of slopes -- every row has glyphs. A per-ELEMENT error can, and the step size says how many elements each row has.
thePerRowLadder.selfControl: electron-against-electron returned shift 0 in every window of every row except 4 windows out of ~500, all in the two topmost bands where the pane header intrudes.

theCause.verdict: A PER-TEXT-ELEMENT WIDTH CEILING IN THE VENDORED gpui-pre CRATE. Not the font, not the advance, not shaping.
theCause.whyThatProducesTHISladder: src/frontend/gpui/app/leaves.nim:1505-1545 splits each code row into a `display: flex` container with ONE SPAN PER TOKEN RUN **plus one span per bracket character**, each `flex-shrink: 0`. Each span is a separate text element, so each one's width is ceil()ed independently and the next span starts at the running sum of ceiled widths. The error accumulates left to right across the row and RESETS at the next row -- which is exactly the measured shape. Chromium accumulates inline run widths in LayoutUnit (1/64 px) with no per-run ceiling, so the reference arm does not.
fourPREDICTIONSandTHEIRmeasurements: A row drawn as ONE text element must not drift. leaves.nim:1542-1544 takes that path when `row.held` is false. MEASURED: several rows have a per-row slope of EXACTLY 0.000%.
The drift must be in whole-ish steps, one per span, not smooth in glyph count. MEASURED: the per-row slopes are discrete and the totals are small integers (0,2,3,4,5,6 device px).

GPUI must be WIDER, never narrower, because ceil only adds. MEASURED: every ladder slope is positive, and rowextent.py's unclipped same-content rows give G-E width of +1 to +5 device px, never negative.

The magnitude must be ~1 device px per span on average (mean ceiling error 0.5 logical px x 2). MEASURED: a row reaching +6 device px. A Python line like `def mul(left, right):` splits into roughly six to eight spans once every bracket becomes its own span.
theCause.whyTHEpaneLEVELslopeDIFFERSbyPANE: because it is an average over rows with different span counts, and the panes hold different code. That is why 0.970/0.727/0.303 was never one number.

whyNoFixWasAttempted.theBriefsINSTRUCTION: 'If the cause turns out to sit in the vendored gpui-pre crate (pinned =0.3.5 from crates.io, with tools/check_gpui_pin.sh keeping three copies of the version in agreement), stop and report rather than forking it.' It does, so this pass stopped.
whyNoFixWasAttempted.thePin: gpui-pre =0.3.5 in rust/gpui-nim-shim/Cargo.toml:97-98 and :124, rust/gpui-kit-probe/Cargo.toml:30, docs/gpui-pin.md:3, plus 80 lines of rust/Cargo.lock. check_gpui_pin.sh exit 0 this pass.
whyNoFixWasAttempted.P1isTHEREFOREunchanged: mean 0.18466 over the three comparable views. The drift ladder did NOT flatten, because nothing was changed that could flatten it. Reporting a flat ladder would have required a fix the brief forbade.

theTHREEroutes_forTheDecisionToCOMEback.route: A -- stop emitting one text element per token.
theTHREEroutes_forTheDecisionToCOMEback.how: gpui-pre already has `StyledText::with_runs(Vec<TextRun>)` (elements/text.rs:526) and `with_highlights` (:433): ONE text element carrying per-range colour. A code row drawn that way is ceil()ed ONCE, so the row carries a single constant sub-pixel offset instead of an accumulating one, and the ladder flattens to a constant. This is the 'derive the rule' option rather than a correction factor: it removes the accumulation instead of compensating for it.
theTHREEroutes_forTheDecisionToCOMEback.cost: the shim has no styled-runs ABI -- `apply_styles_to_div` applies one font-family/colour per element and `gpui_app.rs:638-641` turns a text node into a bare `into_any_element()`. One new element kind and one new FFI shape. Substantial but self-contained, and it also removes the per-bracket span explosion.
theTHREEroutes_forTheDecisionToCOMEback.sideEffect: it would also fix the same accumulation anywhere else a row of styled text is built out of sibling spans.

theTHREEroutes_forTheDecisionToCOMEback.route: B -- a runtime override in the shim.
theTHREEroutes_forTheDecisionToCOMEback.how: the brief notes the shim already carries objc2/objc2-app-kit.
theTHREEroutes_forTheDecisionToCOMEback.assessment: MEASURED AS NOT APPLICABLE to this defect. The ceiling is plain Rust arithmetic inside a non-virtual method of a crate-owned type, reached through gpui's own element tree. There is no Objective-C selector to swizzle and no trait object to substitute. objc2 is the cheaper route for a PLATFORM behaviour; this is not one.

theTHREEroutes_forTheDecisionToCOMEback.route: C -- move the pin, or fork.
theTHREEroutes_forTheDecisionToCOMEback.touches: the three pinned copies plus Cargo.lock.
theTHREEroutes_forTheDecisionToCOMEback.how: whether a later gpui-pre drops the ceil() was NOT checked: only 0.3.5 is in this host's cargo registry and the brief forbids treating the crate as forkable without a decision. Checking upstream is cheap and is the first thing the decision should ask for.

instrumentControls._rule: every instrument this pass used carries a control that would fail if it were broken, and ONE OF THEM DID FAIL AND WAS CAUGHT.
instrumentControls.theOneThatFAILED: the first rowextent.py called a device row 'text' when its summed distance-from-background exceeded 40. Every row cleared that floor -- the pane ground is not flat and 568 columns of small deviations sum past any such threshold. It found ONE band spanning the whole pane and reported a width ratio of exactly 1.0000 on 'every' row: the uniform answer the brief warns is a broken probe until proven otherwise. Its PLANTED control printed BROKEN and the numbers were discarded rather than reported. Counting pixels individually far from the background separates text rows (2-212 ink pixels) from blank ones (0-1) cleanly.
instrumentControls.plantedPeriodControl: advwidth2.py recovers 17.00/18.40/19.30/20.00/21.70 to within 0.01 -- several planted values, because one cannot distinguish 'recovers the answer' from 'always answers that'.
instrumentControls.plantedStretchControl: rowextent.py recovers planted width factors 1.000, 1.005, 1.010 and 1.020 to within 0.004. It reports BAD at 1.040 because 548 x 1.04 overruns the 568-column window, which is the window's limit and not the estimator's; readings were taken only from the passing range.
instrumentControls.selfControl: advance.py and bandladder.py both run the electron profile against itself; it returns shift 0.
instrumentControls.theTYPEcheckPERTURBATION: tsc reported 0 errors in the modified spec and 14 pre-existing errors elsewhere. To prove tsc was actually reading the file, a deliberate type error was inserted: it then reported EXACTLY 1 error in that file, at the inserted line, and the file was restored and byte-compared. Without this the clean result would have been indistinguishable from tsc skipping the file.
instrumentControls.theProbesOWNdefectCAUGHTbyITSownTYPEchec: the first version of the Electron probe guessed Monaco's `EditorOption.fontFamily` id as 51 by analogy with the 75 and 61 already in the file. It recorded `fontFamily: true` on every capture -- 51 is some boolean option. An id naming the wrong option is indistinguishable from a correct one unless the ANSWER is type-checked, so the lookup is now symbolic (window.monaco.editor.EditorOption.fontFamily) and a non-string is rejected. The lane was re-run so the recorded artefact comes from the fixed code.

new.title: gpui-pre ceil()s every text element's width, so a row built from sibling spans accumulates up to 2 device px per span
new.measured: gpui-pre-0.3.5/src/elements/text.rs:765 `size.width = size.width.max(line_size.width).ceil()`. Measured consequence at codetracer 025bd9981 with isonim-gpui ab520c05f: per-row drift of +0 to +6 device px across one editor row, per-row slopes discrete at 0.000/0.278/0.833/1.071/1.290/1.667%, GPUI always wider, while both arms' resolved advance is 9.792 px at 16 px from the same SpaceMono-Regular.ttf.
new.whyItMatters: it is the whole of PARITY-P1's progressive component and it affects any GPUI UI that builds a line of text out of sibling elements, not only the editor.
new.remedy: draw a code row as ONE StyledText with per-range runs (gpui-pre already exposes `with_runs` / `with_highlights`) instead of N sibling spans. Needs a styled-runs ABI in the shim.
new.severity: major for parity, and it is upstream of several smaller readings

new.title: The shim parses and reports letter-spacing but never applies it, and gpui-pre has no letter-spacing at all
new.measured: render_sync.rs:203 parses `letter-spacing` into `styles.letter_spacing` and lib.rs:1446 reports it in the render plan, but no call site applies it; `grep -rn letter_spacing` over gpui-pre-0.3.5/src returns NOTHING, so it cannot currently be applied.
